title: Power Gained by Fluid from Pump or Fan
description: Calculate the power gained by fluid from a pump or fan using mass flow rate and specific work, or alternatively using density, volume flow rate, gravitational acceleration, and head. Multiple formulas are provided for different input scenarios.

components.content: Select the calculation method for power gained by fluid

options.label: Using Mass Flow Rate & Specific Work (P = m·w)
Using Density, Volume Flow & Head (P = ρ·Q·g·h)

outputs.label: Power Gained by Fluid
outputs.formula: inputs.calculation_method === 'method1' ? inputs.mass_flow_rate * inputs.specific_work : inputs.calculation_method === 'method2' ? inputs.density * inputs.volume_flow_rate * inputs.gravitational_acceleration * inputs.head : inputs.calculation_method === 'method3' ? inputs.specific_weight * inputs.volume_flow_rate * inputs.head : inputs.volume_flow_rate * (inputs.pressure_2 - inputs.pressure_1)

outputs.label: Power Gained by Fluid (kW)
outputs.formula: (inputs.calculation_method === 'method1' ? inputs.mass_flow_rate * inputs.specific_work : inputs.calculation_method === 'method2' ? inputs.density * inputs.volume_flow_rate * inputs.gravitational_acceleration * inputs.head : inputs.calculation_method === 'method3' ? inputs.specific_weight * inputs.volume_flow_rate * inputs.head : inputs.volume_flow_rate * (inputs.pressure_2 - inputs.pressure_1)) / 1000

components.content:
## Formulas Used

**Method 1:** P = m·w
- P = power (W)
- m = mass flow rate (kg/s)
- w = specific work (J/kg)

**Method 2:** P = ρ·Q·g·h
- ρ = density (kg/m³)
- Q = volume flow rate (m³/s)
- g = gravitational acceleration (9.81 m/s²)
- h = head (m)

**Method 3:** P = γ·Q·h
- γ = specific weight (N/m³)
- Q = volume flow rate (m³/s)
- h = head (m)

**Method 4:** P = Q·(p₂ - p₁)
- Q = volume flow rate (m³/s)
- p₂ = outlet pressure (Pa)
- p₁ = inlet pressure (Pa)
